Model-average marginal posterior distributions

Source: R/marginal-posterior.R
marginal_posterior.Rd

Creates marginal model-averages posterior distributions for a given parameter based on model-averaged posterior samples and parameter name (and formula with at specification).

marginal_posterior(
  samples,
  parameter,
  formula = NULL,
  at = NULL,
  prior_samples = FALSE,
  use_formula = TRUE,
  transformation = NULL,
  transformation_arguments = NULL,
  transformation_settings = FALSE,
  n_samples = 10000,
  ...
)

Arguments

samples

model-averaged posterior samples created by mix_posteriors(). Mixed factor posteriors that lack the factor metadata of this version of BayesTools (such as those created by BayesTools 0.3.0) must be recreated from models fitted with this version: they stop with an error of class BayesTools_refit_required (see JAGS_validate_fit_contract()). With use_formula = TRUE and no attached formula state, orthonormal or mean-difference factor posteriors whose stored contrast basis differs from the current contrasts stop with the same error class; use_formula = FALSE keeps using the stored design.

parameter

parameter of interest

formula

model formula (needs to be specified if parameter was part of a formula)

at

named list with predictor levels of the formula for which marginalization should be performed. Continuous values use fitted/SD units for fitted posterior views and original data units for views created with transform_scaled = TRUE. A manipulated continuous predictor is evaluated at the existing grid c(-1, 0, 1) in those same view units. If a predictor level is missing, 0 is used for continuous predictors, the baseline factor level is used for factors with contrast = "treatment" prior distributions, and the parameter is completely omitted for factors with contrast = "meandif", contrast = "orthonormal", contrast = "independent", and ordered-factor levels. A predictor without its own main-effect term (e.g., x in ~ g + g:x) is handled by the type, levels, and contrast recorded for it in the interaction terms that contain it.

prior_samples

whether marginal prior distributions should be generated

use_formula

whether the parameter should be evaluated as a part of supplied formula

transformation, transformation_arguments

optional transformation of the marginal posterior, applied with posterior_transform() to the untransformed marginal posterior and its metadata. The transformation is validated before the marginal posterior is built.

transformation_settings, ...

not used by marginal_posterior(), which evaluates no plotting grid; transformation_settings is validated as a logical value and ... is ignored.

n_samples

controls the numerical grid used for model-averaged prior densities (a grid has at least 16 points). It is not used when the samples carry a stored prior-density context. For a simple parameter, an explicitly attached prior_density is authoritative and is propagated instead of being reconstructed from prior_list.

Value

marginal_posterior returns a named list of mixed marginal posterior distributions (either vectors or matrices).

Details

When the mixed posterior samples carry deterministic posterior_density, posterior_ordinate, or support metadata (posterior_metadata()), marginal_posterior() propagates matching metadata to the returned marginal posterior. Matching uses the parameter name, list/level names such as theta[A], and conditional metadata when present. Exact support metadata is propagated even when prior_samples = FALSE; requesting prior samples adds prior-density metadata but does not replace already attached posterior support. A transformation is applied by posterior_transform() to the marginal posterior with all its metadata (supports, atoms, prior densities, stored posterior densities and ordinates, and component supports); the mixed posterior samples themselves must be untransformed (samples transformed with posterior_transform() whose prior is their prior_list are refused). If support metadata is absent, support is inferred from prior metadata only when the posterior samples are on the raw, unconditioned prior scale; otherwise the deterministic prior-density context is used so formula-scale transformations and conditional model restrictions are respected. Marginal posteriors with prior samples also record each draw's mixture component and each component's exact support (components metadata): the model of mix_posteriors() ensembles, or the combination of the mixture and spike-and-slab component indicators of a single fit (as_mixed_posteriors()). Savage_Dickey_BF() uses them when the components' supports differ. With log(intercept) formula scaling, the unscaled intercept (transform_scaled samples) is the exp of a linear combination of the fitted coefficients with the log of the fitted intercept: its simple marginal posterior (use_formula = FALSE) takes its prior density and support from the exp of that combination, and the linear predictors of a formula marginal posterior are linear in the same coefficients. Ordered formula projections reuse retained fitted coefficients, totals and allocations, with aligned model and draw rows, from the contributing formula prefixes. Every provided source of a contributing prefix is used; unrelated prefixes are excluded. Scaling is determined separately for each prefix; an unscaled prefix keeps its fitted draws when another prefix is scaled. Scaled mixed posteriors that lack the fitted ordinary coefficients needed by a formula stop with class BayesTools_ordered_coordinates_unavailable (parent BayesTools_ordered_unavailable); recreate the mixed posteriors from the source fits with this version of BayesTools.
